methods.label: Track both position and orientation
methods.explanation:
A rotation turns every part of the figure, including each small shape's edges. A clockwise \(120^\circ\) turn is one-third of a full turn. Tracking the shapes around the center sends the triangle from the top to the lower right, the square from the lower right to the lower left, and the small circle from the lower left to the top. Only choice B has this arrangement.

[Figure 3](figures/1994_AMC_8_Q04_choiceB_fig3.svg)

However, the square must turn too. A \(90^\circ\) turn makes an upright square look upright again, but
\[
120^\circ=90^\circ+30^\circ.
\]
The additional \(30^\circ\) turn makes its edges slant. The square in choice B still has horizontal and vertical edges, so B is not the exact rotated figure. Since every other choice has the shapes in different positions, none of the displayed choices is an exact rotation. Choice B is the intended answer only if the square's orientation error is disregarded.
methods.levelReason: The argument uses elementary spatial reasoning, clockwise turns, and the familiar quarter-turn symmetry of a square, all appropriate for AMC 8.

Consequently no displayed choice is exact, and the solution correctly qualifies B as intended only.
